title: Counter transfer in the breadth-first search machine
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $\mathrm{orc}$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four indices and each finite Boolean word. Let $st$ be a machine state whose 17 natural-number counters are all at most $B$, let $M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory map, and let $p\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $0\le p\le P$ and $st.c_1+st.c\le B$. In the machine defined by the transition rules of the exponential breadth-first search procedure, the configuration starting in the counter-transfer phase with state $st$, memory $M$, and memory-head position $p$ reaches the copy phase for the radius and next-radius counters with the same memory and head position, with counter $c$ reset to $0$ and counter $c_1$ set to $st.c_1+st.c$. Every configuration strictly before that endpoint has all register values at most $B$, has memory-head position between $0$ and $P$, and satisfies the required operand conditions for its active instruction: equality tests compare distinct registers, input-word comparisons occur only on valid encodings, and calls use distinct argument registers.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{orc}$ is a Boolean-valued oracle on four indices and Boolean words
Every counter of $st$ is at most $B$
$M$ is a Boolean-valued map on the integers
